newsitem.title: INDIA: India NALCO to repay debt by Sept 1998.
newsitem.headline: India NALCO to repay debt by Sept 1998.

text.p: India's state-run aluminium maker National Aluminium Co (NALCO) has said it would repay its outstanding foreign debt of 20 billion Japanese yen ($171.3 million) by September, 1998.

"At this point of time, NALCO's debt liability is in the form of 20 billion Japanese yen, scheduled for repayment in September, 1998," NALCO's chairman S.N. Johri told reporters in the eastern city of Bhubaneshwar on Friday.
Johri said the company did not had any domestic debts.
He said NALCO's overseas loan liability had shot up to 23.67 billion rupees in 1991/92 after devaluation of the rupee, causing serious imbalance to its debt-equity ratio.

"Improved performances and better marketing realisations had enabled the company to pre-pay 9.78 billion rupees in addition to the scheduled repayments of 4.39 billion rupees in the last two years," Johri said.

He said NALCO has sought government approval to convert its 25 percent fully-paid equity capital of 12.89 billion rupees in face value into debt with a four year moratorium and another 25 percent into fully redeemable cumulative preference shares.

Johri said a proposal for the second phase of expansion, which envisages increase in metal production capacity to 345,000 tonnes annually from 230,000 tonnes and power generating capacity to 960 megawatt from 720 at a cost of 27.35 billion rupees, was now pending with the government.

The government has already approved NALCO's proposal to expand bauxite mining capacity to 4.8 million tonnes annually from 2.4 million tonnes and alumina production capacity to 1.57 million tonnes per annum from 800,000 tonnes at an estimated cost of 16.65 billion rupees.

NALCO in 1997/98 (April-March) has set a production target of 218,000 tonnes of aluminium, 800,000 tonnes of alumina and 2.4 million tonnes of bauxite, Johri said. NALCO produced 203,650 tonnes of aluminium in 1996/97.
Johri said NALCO plans to set up facilities to manufacture caustic soda, lime, calcinated petroleum coke and aluminium flouride.
NALCO, Asia's largest aluminium maker, has a domestic market share of 35 percent. ($1 = 116.8 Japanese yen = 35.8 rupees)
